title.en: Volume 83 Biographies 8: The Princesses of all Emperors

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu had one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu had one daughter.

sentences.zh: 同安公主，高祖同母媦也。

translations.literal: Princess Tong'an was the wet nurse who shared a mother with Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Tong'an had nursed Emperor Gaozu from the same mother as his own.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wang Yu, prefect of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Yu, prefect of Sui.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，以屬尊進大長公主。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, because of her senior kinship rank she was advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan she was promoted to Grand Princess on account of her eminent station in the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，太宗躬省視，賜縑五百，姆侍皆有賚予。

translations.literal: Once when she fell ill, Emperor Taizong personally went to visit her, bestowed five hundred bolts of silk, and gave rewards to all her nurses and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When she was once ill, Taizong visited her in person, gave her five hundred bolts of silk, and rewarded every nurse and attendant in her household.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, she was granted three hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui she received an income of three hundred taxable households.

translations.literal: She died at the age of eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 裕，隋司徒柬之子，終開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Sui Minister over the Masses Dong; he ended as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, son of the Sui Minister over the Masses Wang Dong, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu had nineteen daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had nineteen daughters.

translations.literal: Princess Changsha was married down to Feng Shaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changsha married Feng Shaoshi.

translations.literal: Princess Xiangyang was married down to Dou Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xiangyang married Dou Dan.

sentences.zh: 平陽昭公主，太穆皇后所生，下嫁柴紹。

translations.literal: Princess Pingyang the Illustrious, born of Empress Taimu, was married down to Chai Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Pingyang the Illustrious, daughter of Empress Taimu, married Chai Shao.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖兵興，主居長安，紹曰：“尊公將以兵清京師，我欲往，恐不能偕，奈何？

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Gaozu raised his army, the princess remained in Chang'an. Shao said, "Your honored father is about to take troops to pacify the capital. I wish to go, but I fear we cannot go together. What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first took up arms, the princess stayed in Chang'an. Chai Shao said, "Your father is marching to clear the capital. I want to join him, but I doubt we can go together—what should we do?"

translations.literal: " The princess said, "You go; I will make my own plan."
translations.idiomatic: " The princess replied, "Go ahead—I will see to myself."

sentences.zh: ”紹詭道走并州，主奔鄠，發家貲招南山亡命，得數百人以應帝。

translations.literal: " Shao took a deceptive route and fled to Bingzhou. The princess fled to Hu County, spent her family wealth to recruit outlaws from the Southern Mountains, and obtained several hundred men to answer the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao slipped away by a roundabout route to Bingzhou. The princess fled to Hu, spent the family fortune to rally fugitives from the Zhongnan hills, and raised several hundred men to support the emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是，名賊何潘仁壁司竹園，殺行人，稱總管，主遣家奴馬三寶喻降之，共攻鄠阝。

translations.literal: Thereupon the notorious bandit He Panren walled himself in Sizhu Garden, killed travelers, and styled himself commander-in-chief. The princess sent her household slave Ma Sanbao to persuade him to submit, and together they attacked Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The famous bandit He Panren had fortified Sizhu Garden, murdered travelers, and proclaimed himself commander. The princess sent her retainer Ma Sanbao to win him over, and they jointly attacked Hu.

sentences.zh: 別部賊李仲文、向善誌、丘師利等各持所領會戲下，因略地盩厔、武功、始平，下之。

translations.literal: Separate bandit bands under Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, and Qiu Shili each led their followers to join her at Huixi, then seized Zhouzhi, Wugong, and Shiping and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebel leaders—Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, and Qiu Shili—each brought their forces to rally under her at Huixi, then overran Zhouzhi, Wugong, and Shiping.

sentences.zh: 乃申法誓眾，禁剽奪，遠近鹹附，勒兵七萬，威振關中。

translations.literal: She then proclaimed laws and swore the host, forbade pillage, and near and far all attached themselves; she mustered seventy thousand troops, and her might shook Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She imposed discipline on the troops, forbade looting, and won adherents from far and near until she fielded seventy thousand men, her prestige shaking all of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 帝度河，紹以數百騎並南山來迎，主引精兵萬人與秦王會渭北。

translations.literal: When the Emperor crossed the river, Shao came with several hundred horsemen along the Southern Mountains to welcome him. The princess led ten thousand picked troops to join the Prince of Qin north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor crossed the Yellow River, Chai Shao came with several hundred riders along the southern hills to meet him, while the princess led ten thousand elite troops to join the Prince of Qin north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 紹及主對置幕府，分定京師，號“娘子軍”。

translations.literal: Shao and the princess set up opposing headquarters and divided the pacification of the capital, and were called the "Army of the Lady."
translations.idiomatic: Chai Shao and the princess established separate command posts to secure the capital together, and their force was known as the "Lady's Army."

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, he rewarded her service without limit.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession, he heaped rewards on her without end for her achievements.

sentences.zh: 武德六年薨，葬加前後部羽葆、鼓吹、大路、麾幢、虎賁、甲卒、班劍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude she died. For her burial were added front and rear escorts with feather banners, martial music, the great carriage road, command pennants, tiger guards, armored soldiers, and ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Wude 6. Her funeral was granted front and rear escorts with feather banners, martial music, the imperial processional road, command pennants, tiger guards, armored troops, and ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 太常議：“婦人葬，古無鼓吹。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies argued, "For a woman's burial, antiquity knows no martial music."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies objected: "Women's funerals in antiquity did not use martial music."

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not agree and said, "Martial music is army music.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused and said, "Martial music is military music.

sentences.zh: 往者主身執金鼓，參佐命，於古有邪？

translations.literal: In the past the princess herself bore the gongs and drums and took part in establishing the mandate—was there such a thing in antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: The princess herself once wielded gongs and drums and helped win the throne—was there ever such a precedent?

translations.literal: It is fitting to use it.
translations.idiomatic: It is right to use it.

sentences.zh: 高密公主，下嫁長孫孝政，又嫁段綸。

translations.literal: Princess Gaomi was married down to Zhangsun Xiaozheng, and later to Duan Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Gaomi married Zhangsun Xiaozheng and later Duan Lun.

sentences.zh: 綸，隋兵部尚書文振子，為工部尚書、杞國公。

translations.literal: Lun was the son of Sui Minister of War Wen Zhen; he became Minister of Works and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lun, son of the Sui Minister of War Duan Wenzhen, served as Minister of Works and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年主薨，遺命：“吾葬必令墓東向，以望獻陵，冀不忘孝也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui the princess died. Her final command was, "When I am buried, my tomb must face east so that it looks toward Xian Mausoleum, in hope that filial piety will not be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: She died in Yonghui 6, leaving instructions: "Bury me with my tomb facing east toward Xian Mausoleum, so I may never forget my filial duty."

translations.literal: Princess Changgang was first enfeoffed as Princess of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changgang was first created Princess of Guiyang.

translations.literal: She was married down to Zhao Cijing.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zhao Cijing.

sentences.zh: 慈景，隴西人，帝美其姿制，故妻之。

translations.literal: Cijing was a man of Longxi. The Emperor admired his bearing and appearance, and therefore gave him the princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cijing was from Longxi. The emperor admired his looks and manner and gave him the princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝起兵，或勸亡去，對曰：“母以我為命，且安往？

translations.literal: When the Emperor raised his army, some urged him to flee. He replied, "My mother holds me as her very life—where could I go?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took up arms, some urged Cijing to flee. He answered, "My mother lives for me—where would I go?"

translations.literal: " Officials seized and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The authorities arrested and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 帝平京師，引拜開化郡公，為相國府文學。

translations.literal: When the Emperor pacified the capital, he summoned and appointed him Duke of Kaihua and made him literary officer in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was taken, the emperor appointed him Duke of Kaihua and literary officer in the chancellor's office.

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war.

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 討堯君素戰死、贈秦州刺史，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Yao Junsu he died in battle; posthumously he was made prefect of Qin Prefecture, with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died fighting Yao Junsu and was posthumously made prefect of Qin with the posthumous name Loyal.

translations.literal: The princess remarried Yang Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: The princess later married Yang Shidao.

sentences.zh: 聰悟有思，工為詩，豪侈自肆，晚稍折節，以壽薨。

translations.literal: She was clever and thoughtful, skilled at poetry, extravagant and unrestrained; in her later years she somewhat restrained herself, and died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and thoughtful, skilled in poetry, she lived lavishly in her youth but moderated herself in later years and died at an advanced age.

translations.literal: Princess Changsha was first enfeoffed as Princess of Wanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changsha was first created Princess of Wanchun.

translations.literal: She was married down to Dou Lu Huairang, son of Dou Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: She married Dou Huairang, son of Dou Kuan.

translations.literal: Princess Fangling was first enfeoffed as Princess of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Fangling was first created Princess of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 下嫁竇奉節，又嫁賀蘭僧伽。

translations.literal: She was married down to Dou Fengjie, and later to Helan Sengqie.
translations.idiomatic: She married Dou Fengjie and later Helan Sengqie.

sentences.zh: 九江公主，下嫁執失思力。

translations.literal: Princess Jiujiang was married down to Zhishi Sili.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jiujiang married Zhishi Sili.

sentences.zh: 廬陵公主，下嫁喬師望，為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Princess Luling was married down to Qiao Shiwang, who became prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Luling married Qiao Shiwang, who served as prefect of Tong.

translations.literal: Princess Nanchang was married down to Su Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Nanchang married Su Xu.

translations.literal: Princess Anping was married down to Yang Sijing.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anping married Yang Sijing.

translations.literal: Princess Huainan was married down to Feng Daoyan.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Huainan married Feng Daoyan.

translations.literal: Princess Zhending was married down to Cui Gongli.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Zhending married Cui Gongli.

sentences.zh: 衡陽公主，下嫁阿史那社爾。

translations.literal: Princess Hengyang was married down to Ashina She'er.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Hengyang married Ashina She'er.

translations.literal: Princess Danyang was married down to Xue Wanche.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Danyang married Xue Wanche.

sentences.zh: 萬徹蠢甚，公主羞，不與同席者數月。

translations.literal: Wanche was extremely crude. The princess was ashamed and would not share a seat with him for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche was so boorish that the princess, ashamed, refused to sit with him for months.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞，笑焉，為置酒，悉召它婿與萬徹從容語，握槊賭所佩刀，陽不勝，遂解賜之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong heard of it he laughed, set out wine, summoned all the other sons-in-law to converse at ease with Wanche, and played pitch-pot wagering their belt knives. Pretending to lose, he then unfastened his and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard and laughed, held a banquet, called in the other sons-in-law to chat easily with Wanche, and played pitch-pot for their belt knives—feigning defeat, he then gave Wanche his own knife.

translations.literal: The princess rejoiced and ordered that they ride home together in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the princess had them ride home together in one carriage.

translations.literal: Princess Linhai was married down to Pei Lüshi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Linhai married Pei Lüshi.

translations.literal: Princess Guantao was married down to Cui Xuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Guantao married Cui Xuanqing.

translations.literal: Princess Anding was first enfeoffed as Princess of Qianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anding was first created Princess of Qianjin.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wen Ting.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wen Ting.

translations.literal: When Ting died, she remarried Zheng Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Ting's death she married Zheng Jingxuan.

translations.literal: Princess Changle was married down to Zhao Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changle married Zhao Gui.

sentences.zh: 生女，為周王妃，武后殺之。

translations.literal: She bore a daughter who became consort of the Prince of Zhou; Empress Wu killed her.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a daughter who became consort to the Prince of Zhou; Wu Zetian had her killed.

translations.literal: Gui was expelled from his post as prefect of Kuozhou and transferred to Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui was removed as prefect of Kuozhou and exiled to Shou.

sentences.zh: 越王貞將舉兵，遺瑰書假道，瑰將應之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yue, Zhen, was about to raise troops, he sent Gui a letter asking passage through his territory; Gui was about to comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen of Yue prepared to rise in arms, he wrote Zhao Gui asking free passage, and Gui was ready to agree.

sentences.zh: 主進使者曰：“為我謝王，與其進，不與其退。

translations.literal: The princess sent the envoy forward and said, "Bear my thanks to the prince: grant him passage, not refusal."
translations.idiomatic: The princess sent the messenger back with word: "Tell the prince for me—let him advance, do not turn him away."

sentences.zh: 若諸王皆丈夫，不應掩久至是。

translations.literal: If all the princes are truly men, they ought not to have lain low so long as this.
translations.idiomatic: If the princes are truly men of spirit, they should not have waited in hiding this long.

sentences.zh: 我聞楊氏篡周，尉遲迥乃周出，猶能連突厥，使天下響震，況諸王國懿親，宗社所托，不舍生取義，尚何須邪？

translations.literal: I have heard that when the Yang house usurped Zhou, Yuwen Jiong, though only a Zhou clansman, still could link with the Turks and make the realm tremble—how much more you princes, the state's closest kin on whom altar and ancestral temple depend: if you will not give your lives for righteousness, what more is there to wait for?
translations.idiomatic: When the Yang seized Zhou, Yuwen Jiong—only a kinsman of that house—still rallied the Turks and shook the empire. You are the dynasty's closest kin, the pillars of the state—if you will not die for the right, what are you waiting for?

sentences.zh: 人臣同國患為忠，不同為逆，王等勉之。

translations.literal: A subject who shares the state's peril is loyal; one who does not is a rebel. Princes, take heart."
translations.idiomatic: A minister who shares the nation's danger is loyal; one who does not is a traitor. Princes, exert yourselves."

sentences.zh: ”王敗，周興劾瑰與主連謀，皆被殺。

translations.literal: " When the prince was defeated, Zhou Xing impeached Gui and the princess for conspiracy; both were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: " When the prince was defeated, Zhou Xing charged Gui and the princess with conspiracy, and both were executed.

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong had twenty-one daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had twenty-one daughters.

translations.literal: Princess Xiangcheng was married down to Xiao Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xiangcheng married Xiao Rui.

sentences.zh: 性孝睦，動循矩法，帝敕諸公主視為師式。

translations.literal: By nature filial and harmonious, in every act she followed the rules. The Emperor ordered all princesses to take her as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and harmonious by nature, she observed propriety in all things, and the emperor told the other princesses to take her as their example.

sentences.zh: 有司告營別第，辭曰：“婦事舅姑如父母，異宮則定省闕。

translations.literal: When the authorities reported that she was building a separate residence, she declined, saying, "A wife serves her husband's parents as she does her own; in a separate dwelling the morning and evening visits would be wanting."
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported she was building a separate mansion, she refused: "A wife serves her parents-in-law as her own parents—in another house I could not attend them morning and evening."

translations.literal: " She only repaired her old residence and set paired halberds at the gate, and no more.
translations.idiomatic: " She merely repaired her old house and placed paired halberds at the gate—nothing more.

translations.literal: When Rui died, she remarried Jiang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After Rui's death she married Jiang Jian.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年薨，高宗舉哀於命婦朝堂，遣工部侍郎丘行淹馳驛吊祭，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui she died. Emperor Gaozong held mourning for her in the Hall of Court Ladies, sent Vice Minister of Works Qiu Xingyan by post-horse to offer condolences, and had her buried beside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Yonghui 2. Gaozong mourned her in the hall of titled ladies, sent Vice Minister Qiu Xingyan post-haste to offer rites, and had her interred at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 喪次故城，帝登樓望哭以送柩。

translations.literal: The mourning halt was at Gucheng. The Emperor ascended a tower, looked out, and wept as the bier departed.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral procession paused at Gucheng; the emperor climbed a tower, looked out, and wept as the coffin passed.

translations.literal: Princess Runan died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Runan died in youth.

sentences.zh: 南平公主，下嫁王敬直，以累斥嶺南，更嫁劉玄意。

translations.literal: Princess Nanping was married down to Wang Jingzhi; because of his involvement in a case he was banished to Lingnan, and she remarried Liu Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Nanping married Wang Jingzhi; after he was implicated and exiled to Lingnan, she married Liu Xuanyi.

translations.literal: Princess Suian was married down to Dou Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Suian married Dou Kui.

translations.literal: When Kui died, she remarried Wang Dali.
translations.idiomatic: After Kui's death she married Wang Dali.

translations.literal: Princess Changle was married down to Zhangsun Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changle married Zhangsun Chong.

sentences.zh: 帝以長孫皇后所生，故敕有司裝賫視長公主而倍之。

translations.literal: Because she was born of Empress Zhangsun, the Emperor ordered the authorities to prepare her marriage gifts at double the scale set for a chief princess.
translations.idiomatic: Because she was the daughter of Empress Zhangsun, the emperor ordered her dowry prepared at twice the amount given a chief princess.

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：“昔漢明帝封諸王曰：‘朕子安得同先帝子乎？

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said, "In the past Emperor Ming of Han enfeoffed his princes and said, 'How can my sons be treated the same as my father's sons?'"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "When Emperor Ming of Han enfeoffed his sons, he declared, 'How can my sons rank with my father's sons?'"

translations.literal: ' Thus a chief princess is a princess of higher rank.
translations.idiomatic: ' A chief princess, then, outranks an ordinary princess.

translations.literal: Regulations have gradations—how can one overstep them?
translations.idiomatic: The regulations set ranks apart—how can we overstep them?

sentences.zh: ”帝以語后，后曰：“嘗聞陛下厚禮徵而未知也，今聞其言，乃納主於義，社稷臣也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor told the Empress. The Empress said, "I had heard that Your Majesty treated Zheng generously but did not know why. Now hearing his words, I see he keeps the princess within propriety—he is a pillar of the state."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor told the empress. She said, "I knew you honored Wei Zheng but not why. Hearing him now, I see he keeps the princess within right measure—he is a true servant of the realm."

sentences.zh: 妾於陛下，夫婦之重，有所言，猶候顏色，況臣下情隔禮殊，而敢犯嚴顏陳忠言哉！

translations.literal: I, your consort, share the weight of husband and wife with Your Majesty; when I speak I still watch your countenance—how much more a subject, separated by feeling and by ritual, who dares face your stern visage and offer loyal counsel!
translations.idiomatic: Even I, your wife, must read your mood before I speak—how much harder for a subject, divided from you by rank and ritual, to risk your displeasure with honest counsel!

translations.literal: I beg that you grant his request and share the realm's good with all.
translations.idiomatic: Please grant his request and show the realm you hold the public good above private favor.

sentences.zh: ”帝大悅，因請賫帛四十匹、錢四十萬即徵家賜之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly pleased and at once sent forty bolts of silk and four hundred thousand cash to Zheng's house as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted and immediately sent forty bolts of silk and four hundred thousand cash to Wei Zheng's home as a reward.

translations.literal: Princess Yuzhang was married down to Tang Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yuzhang married Tang Yishi.

translations.literal: Princess Beijing was first enfeoffed as Princess of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Beijing was first created Princess of Baling.

sentences.zh: 下嫁柴令武，坐與房遺愛謀反，同主賜死。

translations.literal: She was married down to Chai Lingwu. Because of his involvement in the plot with Fang Yiai, she and the princess were ordered to die by imperial gift.
translations.idiomatic: She married Chai Lingwu. When he was implicated in Fang Yiai's conspiracy, she was ordered to take her own life along with him.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中追贈，立廟於墓，四時祭以少牢。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era she was posthumously ennobled; a temple was erected at her tomb, and in the four seasons she was sacrificed to with the secondary victim set.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing she was posthumously honored, a shrine was built at her tomb, and seasonal offerings of the secondary victim set were made.

translations.literal: Princess Pu'an was married down to Shi Renbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Pu'an married Shi Renbiao.

translations.literal: Princess Dongyang was married down to Gao Lüxing.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Dongyang married Gao Lüxing.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進為大長公主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded, she was promoted to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 韋正矩之誅，主坐婚家，斥徙集州。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhengju was executed, the princess was implicated through her husband's family and was banished to Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhengju was put to death, the princess was punished through her husband's kin and exiled to Ji.

sentences.zh: 又坐章懷太子累，奪邑封。

translations.literal: She was also implicated in the case of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, and her fief income was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: She was further implicated through Crown Prince Zhanghuai and stripped of her fief.

sentences.zh: 以長孫無忌舅族也，故武后惡之，垂拱中，並二子徙置巫州。

translations.literal: Because she was of the maternal clan of Zhangsun Wuji, Empress Wu hated her; in the Chuigong era she and her two sons were banished and resettled in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As kin of Zhangsun Wuji, she was hated by Wu Zetian; in Chuigong she and her two sons were exiled to Wu.

translations.literal: Princess Linchuan was born of Noble Consort Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Linchuan was the daughter of Noble Consort Wei.

translations.literal: She was married down to Zhou Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zhou Daowu.

translations.literal: The princess was skilled in seal and clerical scripts and could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in seal and clerical script and could write essays.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，上《孝德頌》，帝下詔褒答。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, she presented an "Ode to Filial Virtue"; the Emperor issued an edict praising and answering her.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded, she submitted an "Ode to Filial Virtue," and the emperor issued an edict in praise.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，進長公主，恩賞卓異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui she was advanced to chief princess, with extraordinary favor and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui she was promoted to chief princess and received exceptional honors.

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yongchun she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the opening of Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 道務，殿中大監、譙郡公範之子。

translations.literal: Daowu was the son of Zhou Fan, Grand Master of the Palace and Duke of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Daowu was the son of Zhou Fan, palace grand master and Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 初，道務孺褓時，以功臣子養宮中。

translations.literal: At first, when Daowu was still in swaddling clothes, as the son of a meritorious minister he was reared in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: As an infant, being a meritorious minister's son, he was raised in the palace.

translations.literal: When Fan died, he returned to his residence and wasted away in grief like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan died, he went home and mourned with the emaciation of a grown man.

translations.literal: He was brought back inside; only at the age of fourteen was he allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken back into the palace and was not allowed out until he was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 歷營州都督，檢校右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: He served as military governor of Ying Prefecture and acting general of the Right Brave Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Ying and acting general of the Right Brave Guards.

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 清河公主名敬，字德賢，下嫁程懷亮，薨麟德時，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Princess Qinghe, personal name Jing, courtesy name Dexian, was married down to Cheng Huailiang; she died in the Longde era and was buried beside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qinghe, named Jing, courtesy name Dexian, married Cheng Huailiang; she died in Longde and was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 懷亮，知節子也，終寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: Huailiang was the son of Cheng Zhijie and ended as general of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Huailiang, son of Cheng Zhijie, rose to general of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 蘭陵公主名淑，字麗貞，下嫁竇懷悊，薨顯慶時。

translations.literal: Princess Lanling, personal name Shu, courtesy name Lizhen, was married down to Dou Huaizhi; she died in the Xianqing era.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lanling, named Shu, courtesy name Lizhen, married Dou Huaizhi and died in Xianqing.

sentences.zh: 懷悊官兗州都督，太穆皇后之族子。

translations.literal: Huaizhi was military governor of Yan Prefecture and a clansman of Empress Taimu on the maternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Huaizhi served as governor of Yan and was a maternal kinsman of Empress Taimu.

sentences.zh: 晉安公主，下嫁韋思安，又嫁楊仁輅。

translations.literal: Princess Jin'an was married down to Wei Si'an, and later to Yang Renyu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jin'an married Wei Si'an and later Yang Renyu.

translations.literal: Princess Ankang was married down to Dugu Mou.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Ankang married Dugu Mou.

translations.literal: Princess Xinxing was married down to Zhangsun Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xinxing married Zhangsun Xi.

sentences.zh: 城陽公主，下嫁杜荷，坐太子承乾事誅，又嫁薛瓘。

translations.literal: Princess Chengyang was married down to Du He; because of his involvement in Crown Prince Chenghan's affair he was executed, and she remarried Xue Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Chengyang married Du He, who was executed in the Chenghan crown prince affair; she then married Xue Guan.

sentences.zh: 初，主之婚，帝使卜之，繇曰：“二火皆食，始同榮，末同戚，請晝昏則吉。

translations.literal: At first, for the princess's marriage the Emperor had it divined. The line said, "Two fires both feed; at first they share glory, at the end they share sorrow. Request a daytime wedding and it will be auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: When the princess was to marry, the emperor had the matter divined. The oracle read: "Two fires both consume—first shared glory, then shared grief. Marry in daylight and it will be auspicious."

sentences.zh: ”馬周諫曰：“朝謁以朝，思相戒也；

translations.literal: " Ma Zhou remonstrated, saying, "Court audiences are held in the morning so that minds may warn one another;"
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Zhou objected: "Audiences are held at dawn so that minds may admonish one another;"

translations.literal: instruction and study take place in the daytime so that minds may complete one another;
translations.idiomatic: study takes place by day so that minds may strengthen one another;"

translations.literal: feasts and drinking take place in the late afternoon so that minds may rejoice together;
translations.idiomatic: feasts belong to late afternoon so that minds may rejoice together;"

translations.literal: marriage union takes place at night so that minds may draw near one another.
translations.idiomatic: marriage belongs to night so that husband and wife may draw near."

sentences.zh: 故上下有成，內外有親，動息有時，吉兇有儀。

translations.literal: Thus above and below achieve completion, inside and outside have kinship, movement and rest have their seasons, and auspice and misfortune have their rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thus superiors and inferiors are fulfilled, inner and outer are joined, activity and rest keep their seasons, and fortune and misfortune keep their forms.

translations.literal: Now to disorder the beginning first cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: To overturn the beginning of the rite cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 夫卜所以決疑，若黷禮慢先，聖人所不用。

translations.literal: Divination is for resolving doubt; if one profanes ritual and slight the ancestors, the sages do not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Divination resolves doubt; profaning ritual and slighting the ancients is what the sages reject.

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，瓘歷左奉宸衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Longde, Guan served as general of the Left Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longde, Xue Guan served as general of the Left Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 主坐巫蠱，斥瓘房州刺史，主從之官。

translations.literal: The princess was implicated in witchcraft; Guan was demoted to prefect of Fang Prefecture, and the princess followed him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in sorcery, Guan was demoted to prefect of Fang and the princess accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，主薨而瓘卒，雙柩還京師。

translations.literal: In the Xianhe era the princess died and Guan died as well; the two coffins were returned to the capital together.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe the princess died and Guan died too; both coffins were brought back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 子顗，封河東縣侯、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Their son Yan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong and served as prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their son Yan was made Marquis of Hedong and prefect of Ji.

sentences.zh: 瑯邪王沖起兵，顗與弟紹以所部庸、調作兵募士，且應之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Langye, Chong, raised troops, Yan and his younger brother Shao used corvée and tax quotas from their jurisdiction to raise soldiers and were about to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chong of Langye rebelled, Yan and his brother Shao used labor and tax levies to raise troops and prepared to join him.

translations.literal: When Chong was defeated, they killed the prefectural clerk to silence witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong's defeat they killed the prefectural clerk to cover their tracks.

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; they were imprisoned and both put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, both were imprisoned and executed.

translations.literal: Princess Hepu was first enfeoffed as Princess of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Hepu was first created Princess of Gaoyang.

translations.literal: She was married down to Fang Yiai, son of Fang Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: She married Fang Yiai, son of Fang Xuanling.

translations.literal: The princess was beloved by the Emperor, and therefore the rites for her husband differed from other sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored her, so her husband was treated unlike other imperial sons-in-law.

translations.literal: Relying on the Emperor's love, the princess grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in the emperor's affection, she grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 房遺直以嫡當拜銀青光祿大夫，讓弟遺愛，帝不許。

translations.literal: Fang Yizhi, as the legitimate son, should have been appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace; he yielded the post to his younger brother Yiai, but the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yizhi, the eldest son, was entitled to the Silver-Gleam Grand Master post but yielded it to Yiai; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 玄齡卒，主導遺愛異貲，既而反譖之，遺直自言，帝痛讓主，乃免。

translations.literal: When Xuanling died, the princess led Yiai to divide the estate unequally; afterward she slandered Yizhi in return. Yizhi spoke for himself, and the Emperor sternly reproached the princess, then pardoned Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanling's death the princess helped Yiai seize an unfair share of the estate, then slandered Yizhi; when Yizhi appealed, the emperor rebuked the princess and excused Yizhi.

translations.literal: From then on she was somewhat estranged; the princess was resentful.
translations.idiomatic: After that she was kept at a distance, and the princess brooded.

sentences.zh: 會御史劾盜，得浮屠辯機金寶神枕，自言主所賜。

translations.literal: It happened that the censor impeached a theft and obtained from the monk Bianji golden treasures and a divine pillow, which he said the princess had bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor investigated theft, he found on the monk Bianji gold, jewels, and a divine pillow that Bianji said the princess had given him.

sentences.zh: 初，浮屠廬主之封地，會主與遺愛獵，見而悅之，具帳其廬，與之亂，更以二女子從遺愛，私餉億計。

translations.literal: At first the monk had dwelt on the princess's fief. Once when the princess and Yiai were hunting, she saw him and was pleased; she set up a full camp at his hut, had an affair with him, and gave Yiai two women in exchange, privately bestowing on him sums in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Bianji had lived on her estate; she met him while hunting, favored him, lodged with him, took him as lover, gave Yiai two women in exchange, and secretly lavished vast sums on him.

sentences.zh: 至是，浮屠殊死，殺奴婢十余。

translations.literal: At this time the monk was executed by dismemberment, and more than ten slave girls were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bianji was executed by dismemberment and more than ten slave girls were put to death.

translations.literal: The princess grew still more resentful and showed no mourning countenance when the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: She grew more bitter still and showed no grief when the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 又浮屠智勖迎占禍福，惠弘能視鬼，道士李晃高醫，皆私侍主。

translations.literal: Moreover the monk Zhi Xu practiced divination for fortune and misfortune, Hui Hong could see ghosts, and the Daoist Li Huang was a skilled physician—all privately attended the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhi Xu divined fortunes, Hui Hong claimed to see ghosts, and the Daoist Li Huang practiced medicine—all served her in secret.

sentences.zh: 主使掖廷令陳玄運伺宮省禨祥，步星次。

translations.literal: The princess had the Palace Revenues Director Chen Xuanyun spy on omens within the palace and pace the stars.
translations.idiomatic: She had Chen Xuanyun, director of palace revenues, watch palace omens and track the stars.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，與遺愛謀反，賜死。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era she plotted rebellion with Yiai and was ordered to die by imperial gift.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui she conspired with Yiai and was ordered to take her own life.

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era she was posthumously ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing she was posthumously honored.

translations.literal: Princess Jinshan died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jinshan died in youth.

sentences.zh: 晉陽公主字明達，幼字兕子，文德皇后所生。

translations.literal: Princess Jinyang, courtesy name Mingda, childhood name Zizi, was born of Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jinyang, courtesy name Mingda, childhood name Zizi, was the daughter of Empress Wende.

translations.literal: She was never seen to show joy or anger on her face.
translations.idiomatic: She never showed joy or anger on her face.

sentences.zh: 帝有所怒責，必伺顏徐徐辯解，故省中多蒙其惠，莫不譽愛。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was angry and reproached someone, she would watch his expression and slowly argue in explanation; therefore many in the inner quarters received her kindness, and none did not praise and love her.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew angry, she watched his mood and gently pleaded for the accused, winning gratitude throughout the inner palace.

translations.literal: When the Empress died, the princess was still an infant and did not know her;
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died the princess was still an infant and did not know her;

sentences.zh: 及五歲，經后所遊地，哀不自勝。

translations.literal: when she reached five years and passed places the Empress had visited, her grief was beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: at five, passing places her mother had frequented, she grieved beyond control.

sentences.zh: 帝諸子，唯晉王及主最少，故親畜之。

translations.literal: Among the Emperor's sons, only the Prince of Jin and the princess were youngest, and therefore he cherished them closely.
translations.idiomatic: Of the emperor's sons only the Prince of Jin and the princess were youngest, and he kept them especially close.

sentences.zh: 王每出閤，主送至虔化門；

translations.literal: Whenever the prince left the inner quarters, the princess escorted him to Qianhua Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince left the palace, the princess walked with him to Qianhua Gate;

translations.literal: they parted in tears.
translations.idiomatic: they parted in tears.

sentences.zh: 王勝衣，班於朝，主泣曰：“兄今與群臣同列，不得在內乎？

translations.literal: When the prince came of age and took his place at court, the princess wept and said, "Elder brother now stands with the ministers in rank—can he no longer remain within?"
translations.idiomatic: When the prince came of age and attended court, she wept: "Brother now ranks with the ministers—can he no longer stay within?"

translations.literal: " The Emperor also shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept as well.

sentences.zh: 主臨帝飛白書，下不能辨。

translations.literal: When the princess faced the Emperor's flying-white calligraphy, her subordinates could not distinguish it.
translations.idiomatic: When she copied the emperor's flying-white calligraphy, her attendants could not tell it from his hand.

translations.literal: She died at the age of twelve.
translations.idiomatic: She died at twelve.

sentences.zh: 帝閱三旬不常膳，日數十哀，因以臒羸。

translations.literal: The Emperor went more than thirty days without regular meals, grieving dozens of times a day, and thereby grew thin and weak.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty days the emperor scarcely ate, grieving many times daily until he grew gaunt.

sentences.zh: 群臣進勉，帝曰：“朕渠不知悲愛無益？

translations.literal: The ministers urged him to take heart. The Emperor said, "Do I not know that grief and love are of no use?"
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged restraint. The emperor said, "Do I not know mourning avails nothing?"

sentences.zh: 而不能已，我亦不知其所以然。

translations.literal: Yet I cannot stop; I too do not know why it is so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I cannot stop—I do not know why myself.

sentences.zh: ”因詔有司簿主湯沐余貲，營佛祠墓側。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the authorities to record the princess's remaining bath-and-income funds and build a Buddhist shrine beside her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered her remaining income recorded and a Buddhist shrine built beside her tomb.

sentences.zh: 常山公主，未及下嫁，薨顯慶時。

translations.literal: Princess Changshan died in the Xianqing era before her marriage could be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changshan died in Xianqing before she could marry.

translations.literal: Princess Xincheng was the younger sister of Jinyang by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xincheng was Jinyang's younger sister by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 下嫁長孫詮，詮以罪徙巂州。

translations.literal: She was married down to Zhangsun Quan; Quan was banished to Xizhou for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zhangsun Quan, who was banished to Xizhou for a crime.

sentences.zh: 更嫁韋正矩，為奉冕大夫，遇主不以禮。

translations.literal: She remarried Wei Zhengju, who was a Grand Master of the Court Cap; he did not treat the princess with proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: She then married Wei Zhengju, a court grand master, who failed to treat her with proper respect.

sentences.zh: 俄而主暴薨，高宗詔三司雜治，正矩不能辯，伏誅。

translations.literal: Soon the princess died suddenly. Emperor Gaozong ordered the Three Offices to investigate jointly; Zhengju could not defend himself and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: She soon died suddenly; Gaozong had the Three Offices investigate, Zhengju could not clear himself, and he was executed.

translations.literal: She was buried beside Zhaoling with the rites due an empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried beside Zhaoling with empress-level rites.

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had three daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had three daughters.

sentences.zh: 義陽公主，蕭淑妃所生，下嫁權毅。

translations.literal: Princess Yiyang was born of Consort Xiao Shufei and was married down to Quan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yiyang, daughter of Consort Xiao, married Quan Yi.

translations.literal: Princess Gao'an was the younger sister of Yiyang by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Gao'an was Yiyang's younger sister by the same mother.

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: She was first created Princess of Xuancheng.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wang Xu, prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Xu, prefect of Ying.

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era Xu was executed by Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshou Wang Xu was executed by Wu Zetian.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，進冊長公主，實封千戶，開府置官屬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong she was advanced to chief princess with a substantive fief of a thousand households and an office with staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong she was promoted to chief princess with a thousand-household fief and her own staff.

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, her households were increased by a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong succeeded, her fief was increased by another thousand households.

sentences.zh: 薨開元時，玄宗哭於暉政門，遣大鴻臚持節赴吊，京兆尹攝鴻臚護喪事。

translations.literal: She died in the Kaiyuan era. Emperor Xuanzong wept at Huizheng Gate, sent the Grand Herald with credentials to offer condolences, and had the metropolitan governor act as Grand Herald to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Kaiyuan; Xuanzong wept at Huizheng Gate, sent the Grand Herald to mourn, and had the metropolitan governor oversee the rites.

sentences.zh: 太平公主，則天皇后所生，后愛之傾諸女。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping was born of Empress Zetian; the Empress loved her above all her daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was Wu Zetian's daughter, favored above all her sisters.

sentences.zh: 榮國夫人死，后丐主為道士，以幸冥福。

translations.literal: When Lady Rongguo died, the Empress begged that the princess become a Daoist nun to bring blessings in the nether world.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Rongguo died, the empress had the princess take Daoist orders to bless her in the afterlife.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，吐蕃請主下嫁，后不欲棄之夷，乃真築宮，如方士薰戒，以拒和親事。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era Tibet requested the princess in marriage; the Empress did not wish to give her to the barbarians, and so had a palace truly built and, like a Daoist adept undergoing fumigation and abstinence, refused the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng Tibet sought her hand; unwilling to give her to foreigners, the empress built a palace and, like a Daoist in ritual seclusion, refused the match.

sentences.zh: 久之，主衣紫袍玉帶，折上巾，具紛礪，歌舞帝前。

translations.literal: After a long time the princess wore a purple robe and jade belt, a folded-up kerchief, full armor, and danced before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later she appeared before the emperor in purple robe, jade belt, military cap, full armor, and danced.

sentences.zh: 帝及后大笑曰：“兒不為武官，何遽爾？

translations.literal: The Emperor and Empress laughed greatly and said, "Child, you are no military officer—why so suddenly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress laughed: "Child, you are no soldier—why dress like this?"

translations.literal: " The princess said, "May it be given to a son-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "May this be bestowed on a son-in-law?"

translations.literal: " The Emperor understood her meaning and chose Xue Shao to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor understood and chose Xue Shao as her husband.

sentences.zh: 假萬年縣為婚館，門隘不能容翟車，有司毀垣以入，自興安門設燎相屬，道樾為枯。

translations.literal: They borrowed Wannian County as the wedding hall; the gate was too narrow for the pheasant carriage, and the authorities tore down walls to admit it. From Xing'an Gate torches were set in unbroken succession, and the roadside trees were scorched bare.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian County served as the wedding hall; the gate was too narrow for the bridal carriage and walls were torn down; torches lined the road from Xing'an Gate and scorched the trees bare.

sentences.zh: 紹死，更嫁武承嗣，會承嗣小疾，罷昏。

translations.literal: When Shao died, she remarried Wu Chengsi; Chengsi fell slightly ill and the marriage was called off.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao's death she was to marry Wu Chengsi, but a minor illness canceled the wedding.

translations.literal: The Empress killed Wu Youji's wife and gave her to the princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The empress killed Wu Youji's wife and gave him to the princess.

sentences.zh: 主方額廣頤，多陰謀，后常謂“類我”。

translations.literal: The princess had a broad forehead and full cheeks and many secret schemes; the Empress often said, "She is like me."
translations.idiomatic: Broad-faced and full-cheeked, she was full of intrigue; the empress often said, "She is my likeness."

sentences.zh: 而主內與謀，外檢畏，終後世無它訾。

translations.literal: Yet inwardly she plotted while outwardly she showed restraint and fear, and through her life she received no other blame.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly she plotted, outwardly she was cautious, and she escaped other reproach through her life.

sentences.zh: 永淳之前，親王食實戶八百，增至千輒止；

translations.literal: Before Yongchun, imperial princes received eight hundred substantive households, increased to a thousand and then stopped;
translations.idiomatic: Before Yongchun, princes received eight hundred taxable households, raised to a thousand and no further;

sentences.zh: 公主不過三百，而主獨加戶五十。

translations.literal: princesses received no more than three hundred, but the princess alone was given an additional fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: princesses received no more than three hundred, but she alone received fifty more.

translations.literal: In the Shengli era her fief was advanced to three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengli her fief rose to three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 預誅二張功，增號鎮國，與相王均封五千，而薛、武二家女皆食實封。

translations.literal: For her foresight in executing the Zhang brothers, her title was increased to Pacifier of the State; she and the Prince of Xiang were each granted five thousand households, and the daughters of the Xue and Wu families all received substantive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: For helping eliminate the Zhang brothers, she was titled Pacifier of the State; she and the Prince of Xiang each received five thousand households, and daughters of the Xue and Wu houses held substantive fiefs.

sentences.zh: 主與相王衛王成王、長寧安樂二公主給衛士，環第十步一區，持兵呵衛，僣肖宮省。

translations.literal: The princess, together with the princes of Xiang, Wei, and Cheng and the princesses of Changning and Anle, were given guards; every ten paces around her residence a post was set, armed men shouted warnings, and the display imitated the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: She and the princes of Xiang, Wei, and Cheng plus Princesses Changning and Anle were given guards posted every ten paces, armed escorts, and displays imitating the palace.

sentences.zh: 神龍時，與長寧、安樂、宜城、新都、定安、金城凡七公主，皆開府置官屬，視親王。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era she, together with Changning, Anle, Yicheng, Xindu, Ding'an, and Jincheng—seven princesses in all—each opened an office with staff, treated like imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong she and six other princesses each opened offices with staffs, equal to imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 安樂戶至三千，長寧二千五百，府不置長史。

translations.literal: Anle's households reached three thousand; Changning's two thousand five hundred; their offices did not appoint chief secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Anle held three thousand households, Changning twenty-five hundred; their offices omitted chief secretaries.

sentences.zh: 宜城、定安非韋后所生，戶止二千。

translations.literal: Yicheng and Ding'an were not born of Empress Wei; their households were limited to two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng and Ding'an were not Empress Wei's daughters and received only two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 主三子：崇簡、崇敏、崇行，皆拜三品。

translations.literal: The princess had three sons: Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing—all appointed third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Her three sons Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing were all made third rank.

sentences.zh: 韋后、上官昭容用事，自以謀出主下遠甚，憚之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei and Lady Shangguan Zhaorong held power, they considered their schemes far superior to the princess's and feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei and Lady Shangguan, in power, thought themselves far shrewder than the princess and feared her.

sentences.zh: 主亦自以軋而可勝，故益橫。

translations.literal: The princess also considered herself able to overcome them, and therefore grew still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: The princess believed she could dominate them and grew more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 於是推進天下士，謂儒者多窶狹，厚持金帛謝之，以動大議，遠近翕然響之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she promoted men of talent throughout the realm, saying that Confucians were mostly poor and narrow; she held out gold and silk generously to win them and sway great deliberations, and near and far responded as one.
translations.idiomatic: She promoted scholars nationwide, dismissing Confucians as narrow, lavished gold and silk to sway opinion, and won followers everywhere.

sentences.zh: 玄宗將誅韋氏，主與秘計，遣子崇簡從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was about to execute the Wei clan, the princess joined in secret planning and sent her son Chongjian to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong moved against the Wei clan, she plotted in secret and sent Chongjian with him.

sentences.zh: 事定，將立相王，未有以發其端者。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled and they were about to enthrone the Prince of Xiang, no one had yet found a way to begin.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup, as they prepared to enthrone the Prince of Xiang, no one had opened the way.

sentences.zh: 主顧溫王乃兒子，可劫以為功，乃入見王曰：“天下事歸相王，此非兒所坐。

translations.literal: The princess looked to the Prince of Wen as the Emperor's son and one who could be compelled for merit; she entered to see the prince and said, "The realm's affairs belong to the Prince of Xiang—this is no seat for a child."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Prince of Wen as a pawn, she told him: "The throne belongs to the Prince of Xiang—this is no place for you."

translations.literal: " She then helped the prince down, took the imperial carriage robes, and presented them to Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: " She led him down, took the imperial regalia, and presented them to Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，主權由此震天下，加實封至萬戶，三子封王，余皆祭酒、九卿。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, the princess's power thereby shook the realm; her substantive fief was increased to ten thousand households, her three sons were enfeoffed as princes, and the rest became court academicians and nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong's accession made her power shake the realm: ten thousand households, three sons enfeoffed as princes, others made ministers.

sentences.zh: 主每奏事，漏數徙乃得退，所言皆從。

translations.literal: Whenever the princess presented business, the clepsydra was moved several times before she withdrew; whatever she said was followed.
translations.idiomatic: She lingered over each audience until the water clock was moved repeatedly, and all she said was obeyed.

sentences.zh: 有所論薦，或自寒冗躐進至侍從，旋踵將相。

translations.literal: Those she recommended might leap from humble obscurity to attendant at court and in the turn of a heel become chancellor or general.
translations.idiomatic: Her protégés could rise from obscurity to attendants and within days become chancellors or generals.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大政事非關決不下，聞不朝，則宰相就第咨判，天子殆畫可而已。

translations.literal: Great affairs of state were not settled without her; if she did not attend court, the chancellor went to her residence for consultation and judgment, and the Son of Heaven could only approve in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Major state affairs awaited her word; if she skipped court, chancellors came to her house, and the emperor merely ratified.

sentences.zh: 主侍武后久，善策人主微指，先事逢合，無不中。

translations.literal: Having attended Empress Wu for long, she was skilled at divining the ruler's subtle intent and anticipating events to match them—none failed.
translations.idiomatic: Long at Wu Zetian's side, she read the ruler's mind and anticipated events without fail.

translations.literal: Her fields and gardens spread through the near capital districts, all of the richest soil.
translations.idiomatic: Her estates near the capital were all prime land.

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀、嶺嶠市作器用，州縣護送，道相望也。

translations.literal: From Wu, Shu, and the Ling ranges markets sent crafted goods; prefectures and counties escorted them, and the roads were unbroken with convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, Shu, and the far south sent luxuries under escort, convoys unending on the roads.

sentences.zh: 天下珍滋譎怪充於家，供帳聲伎與天子等。

translations.literal: The rarest delicacies and strangest curiosities of the realm filled her house; her furnishings, music, and performers equaled the Son of Heaven's.
translations.idiomatic: Rare foods and curios filled her house; her retinue and entertainers rivaled the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 侍兒曳紈谷者數百，奴伯嫗監千人，隴右牧馬至萬匹。

translations.literal: Several hundred serving girls trailed silk, more than a thousand male and female stewards supervised them, and horses pastured in Longyou reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of maids trailed silk, a thousand stewards oversaw them, and ten thousand horses grazed in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 長安浮屠慧範畜貲千萬，諧結權近，本善張易之。

translations.literal: The Chang'an monk Huifan amassed wealth in the tens of millions, curried favor with the powerful, and had originally been close to Zhang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huifan of Chang'an amassed tens of millions, curried favor with the powerful, and had been close to Zhang Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 及易之誅，或言其豫謀者，於是封上庸郡公，月給奉稍。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, some said Huifan had taken part in the plot; he was therefore enfeoffed as Duke of Shangyong with a monthly stipend.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhi's death some said Huifan had plotted with him; he was made Duke of Shangyong with a monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 主乳媼與通，奏擢三品御史大夫。

translations.literal: The princess's wet nurse had an affair with him; she memorialized to promote him to third-rank Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Her wet nurse was his lover; she had him promoted to censor-in-chief, third rank.

sentences.zh: 御史魏傳弓劾其奸贓四十萬，請論死。

translations.literal: The censor Wei Chuanggong impeached him for corruption of four hundred thousand and requested the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Chuanggong impeached him for four hundred thousand in graft and sought his execution.

sentences.zh: 中宗欲赦之，進曰：“刑賞，國大事，陛下賞已妄加矣，又欲廢刑，天下其謂何？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong wished to pardon him. Chuanggong advanced and said, "Rewards and punishments are great affairs of state. Your Majesty's rewards have already been rashly bestowed; if you now wish to set aside punishment, what will the realm say?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong wished to pardon him. Wei Chuanggong said: "Rewards and punishments are the state's foundation. You have already rewarded rashly—if you now waive punishment, what will the world say?"

translations.literal: " The Emperor had no choice and stripped Huifan of his silver-blue rank.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had no choice and stripped Huifan of his silver-blue rank.

sentences.zh: 大夫薛謙光劾慧範不法，不可貸，主為申理，故謙光等反得罪。

translations.literal: Grand Master Xue Qianguang impeached Huifan for lawlessness and that he could not be pardoned; the princess pleaded on his behalf, and therefore Qianguang and the others in turn were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qianguang impeached Huifan as beyond pardon; the princess intervened, and Qianguang and others were punished instead.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以太子監國，使宋王、岐王總禁兵。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, as crown prince regent, had the princes of Song and Qi command the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: As regent, Xuanzong had the princes of Song and Qi command the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 主恚權分，乘輦至光範門，召宰相白廢太子。

translations.literal: The princess resented the division of power, rode in her carriage to Guangfan Gate, and summoned the chancellor to announce the deposition of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting shared power, she rode to Guangfan Gate and summoned the chancellor to depose the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 於是宋璟、姚元之不悅，請出主東都，帝不許，詔主居蒲州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song Jing and Yao Yuanzhi were displeased and requested that the princess be sent to the eastern capital; the Emperor did not permit it but ordered her to reside in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Yao Yuanzhi urged sending her to the eastern capital; the emperor refused but sent her to Pu.

sentences.zh: 主大望，太子懼，奏斥璟、元之以銷戢怨嫌。

translations.literal: The princess was greatly resentful; the crown prince feared and memorialized to dismiss Jing and Yuanzhi to ease the enmity.
translations.idiomatic: She was furious; the crown prince, fearing trouble, had Song and Yao dismissed to ease tensions.

sentences.zh: 監察御史慕容珣復劾慧範事，帝疑珣離間骨肉，貶密州司馬。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Murong Xun again impeached Huifan; the Emperor suspected Xun of driving wedges between kin and demoted him to secretary in Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Murong Xun again impeached Huifan; the emperor suspected him of dividing the family and demoted him to Mi.

sentences.zh: 主居外四月，太子表追還京師。

translations.literal: After the princess had lived outside the capital four months, the crown prince memorialized to recall her to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After four months in exile, the crown prince had her recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時宰相七人，五出主門下。

translations.literal: At the time there were seven chancellors; five had come from the princess's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Of seven chancellors, five were her clients.

sentences.zh: 又左羽林大將軍常元楷、知羽林軍李慈皆私謁主。

translations.literal: Moreover the Left General of the Feathered Forest Army Chang Yuankai and the commander of the Feathered Forest Li Ci both paid her private visits.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Chang Yuankai and Li Ci of the Feathered Forest also visited her privately.

sentences.zh: 主內忌太子明，又宰相皆其黨，乃有逆謀。

translations.literal: Inwardly the princess resented the crown prince's brilliance; moreover the chancellors were all her faction—thereupon she formed a treasonous plot.
translations.idiomatic: She hated the brilliant crown prince and, with chancellors in her faction, plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，與尚書左僕射竇懷貞、侍中岑羲、中書令蕭至忠崔湜、太子少保薛稷、雍州長史李晉、右散騎常侍昭文館學士賈膺福、鴻臚卿唐晙及元楷、慈、慧範等謀廢太子，使元楷、慈舉羽林兵入武德殿殺太子，懷貞、羲、至忠舉兵南衙為應。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, together with Left Vice Minister Dou Huaizhen, Palace Attendant Cen Yi, Chancellors Xiao Zhibo and Cui Shi, Crown Prince Tutor Xue Ji, metropolitan governor Li Jin, Right Regular Attendant and Zhaowen Hall academician Jia Yingfu, Grand Herald Tang Jun, and Yuankai, Ci, and Huifan, she plotted to depose the crown prince, having Yuankai and Ci lead Feathered Forest troops into Wude Hall to kill the crown prince while Huaizhen, Yi, and Zhibo raised troops in the southern offices in response.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian 2 she joined Dou Huaizhen, Cen Yi, Xiao Zhibo, Cui Shi, Xue Ji, Li Jin, Jia Yingfu, Tang Jun, Yuankai, Ci, and Huifan to depose the crown prince—Yuankai and Ci would strike Wude Hall while others rose in the southern offices.

sentences.zh: 既有日矣，太子得其奸，召岐王、薛王、兵部尚書郭元振、將軍王毛仲、殿中少監姜晈、中書侍郎王琚、吏部侍郎崔日用定策。

translations.literal: When the day had been set, the crown prince learned of the plot and summoned the princes of Qi and Xue, Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen, General Wang Maochong, Palace Vice Director Jiang Jiao, Vice Minister of the Secretariat Wang Ju, and Vice Minister of the Civil Office Cui Riyong to fix a plan.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the coup the crown prince learned of it and gathered the princes of Qi and Xue, Guo Yuanzhen, Wang Maochong, Jiang Jiao, Wang Ju, and Cui Riyong.

sentences.zh: 前一日，因毛仲取內閑馬三百，率太仆少卿李令問王守一、內侍高力士、果毅李守德叩虔化門，梟元楷、慈於北闕下，縛膺福內客省，執羲、至忠至朝堂，斬之，因大赦天下。

translations.literal: The day before, through Maochong he took three hundred imperial stable horses, and leading Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, eunuch Gao Lishi, and guardsman Li Shoude knocked at Qianhua Gate, beheaded Yuankai and Ci below the northern gate, bound Yingfu in the Inner Guests Office, seized Yi and Zhibo and brought them to the court hall and executed them, then proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, he seized three hundred palace horses, stormed Qianhua Gate, beheaded Yuankai and Ci, seized Yi and Zhibo and executed them at court, and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 主聞變，亡入南山，三日不出，賜死於第。

translations.literal: When the princess heard of the change she fled into the Southern Mountains and for three days did not emerge; she was ordered to die by imperial gift in her residence.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the coup, she fled into the Zhongnan hills; after three days she was ordered to die at home.

sentences.zh: 諸子及黨與死者數十人。

translations.literal: Her sons and party members who died numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of her sons and followers died.

sentences.zh: 簿其田貲，瑰寶若山，督子貸，凡三年不能盡。

translations.literal: When her fields and wealth were inventoried, jewels piled like mountains; her sons were compelled to lend and collect, and in all three years they could not exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: Her assets were inventoried—jewels like mountains—and even three years of forced collection by her sons could not exhaust them.

sentences.zh: 崇簡素知主謀，苦諫，主怒，榜掠尤楚，至是復官爵，賜氏李。

translations.literal: Chongjian had long known the princess's plot and remonstrated bitterly; the princess was angry and had him flogged most cruelly. Now his office and rank were restored and he was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian had warned her and was cruelly flogged; now he was restored and given the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 始，主作觀池樂遊原，以為盛集，既敗，賜寧、申、岐、薛四王，都人歲祓禊其地。

translations.literal: At first the princess had made the Guan Pond at Leyou Plateau her great gathering place; after her defeat it was granted to the princes of Ning, Shen, Qi, and Xue, and the capital people held annual purification rites there.
translations.idiomatic: Her estate at Leyou Plateau was granted to four princes after her fall, and the capital held annual rites there.

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong had eight daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong had eight daughters.

translations.literal: Princess Xindu was married down to Wu Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xindu married Wu Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 宜城公主，始封義安郡主。

translations.literal: Princess Yicheng was first enfeoffed as Princess of Yi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yicheng was first created Princess of Yi'an commandery.

translations.literal: She was married down to Pei Xun.
translations.idiomatic: She married Pei Xun.

sentences.zh: 巽有嬖姝，主恚，刖耳劓鼻，且斷巽發。

translations.literal: Xun had a favorite concubine; the princess was furious, cut off her ears and nose, and also cut off Xun's hair.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun favored a concubine, she cut off the woman's ears and nose and shaved Xun's head.

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, demoted her to county princess, and transferred Xun to a lower post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong demoted her to county princess and demoted Xun.

translations.literal: After a long time her former title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In time her former title was restored.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，與長寧、新寧、義安、安樂、新平五郡主皆進封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong she, together with the five commandery princesses of Changning, Xinning, Yi'an, Anle, and Xinping, were all advanced in enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 she and five other commandery princesses were all promoted in rank.

translations.literal: Princess Ding'an was first enfeoffed as Princess of Xinning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Ding'an was first Princess of Xinning commandery.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wang Tongjiao.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Tongjiao.

sentences.zh: 同皎得罪，神龍時，又嫁韋濯。

translations.literal: When Tongjiao was implicated in a crime, in the Shenlong era she remarried Wei Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongjiao's disgrace in Shenlong she married Wei Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 濯即韋皇后從祖弟，以衛尉少卿誅，更嫁太府卿崔銑。

translations.literal: Zhuo was Empress Wei's cousin on the paternal side; as Vice Director of the Imperial Guard he was executed, and she remarried Cui Xian, Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo, Empress Wei's cousin, was executed as vice director of the guard; she then married Cui Xian, director of the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 主薨，王同皎子請與父合葬，給事中夏侯銛曰：“主義絕王廟，恩成崔室，逝者有知，同皎將拒諸泉。

translations.literal: When the princess died, Wang Tongjiao's son requested burial with his father. The Attendant-in-Ordinary Xia Houqian said, "The princess's bond with the Wang house is severed and her favor rests with the Cui house; if the dead have knowledge, Tongjiao will reject him at the springs."
translations.idiomatic: At her death Tongjiao's son sought joint burial with his father. Xia Houqian said: "She severed ties with the Wangs for the Cuis—if the dead know, Tongjiao will refuse him."

translations.literal: " Xian perhaps appealed to the Emperor, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Xian appealed to the emperor and the request was denied.

translations.literal: Qian was demoted to military governor of Lu Prefecture for this.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Houqian was demoted to governor of Lu for this.

sentences.zh: 長寧公主，韋庶人所生，下嫁楊慎交。

translations.literal: Princess Changning was born of the commoner consort Wei and was married down to Yang Shenjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changning, daughter of Consort Wei, married Yang Shenjiao.

sentences.zh: 造第東都，使楊務廉營總。

translations.literal: She built a residence in the eastern capital and had Yang Wulian oversee the work in total.
translations.idiomatic: She built a mansion in Luoyang under Yang Wulian's direction.

sentences.zh: 第成，府財幾竭，乃擢務廉將作大匠。

translations.literal: When the residence was finished the prefectural treasury was nearly exhausted, and Wulian was promoted to Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished the treasury was nearly drained and Wulian was made Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 又取西京高士廉第、左金吾衛故營合為宅，右屬都城，左頫大道，作三重樓以馮觀，築山浚池。

translations.literal: She also took the western capital residence of Gao Shilian and the old camp of the Left Golden Guard and combined them into one mansion: on the right it bordered the capital, on the left it overlooked the great avenue; she built triple towers for viewing, piled mountains and dredged pools.
translations.idiomatic: She seized Gao Shilian's western capital mansion and the Left Golden Guard's old camp, built triple towers, artificial hills, and ponds.

sentences.zh: 帝及后數臨幸，置酒賦詩。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Empress visited several times, set out wine, and composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress visited repeatedly for feasts and poetry.

translations.literal: She also annexed vacant land west of the ward to expand the cuju field.
translations.idiomatic: She expanded the polo ground by annexing vacant land west of the ward.

sentences.zh: 東都廢永昌縣，主丐其治為府，以地瀕洛，築鄣之，崇臺、蜚觀相聯屬。

translations.literal: In the eastern capital Yongchang County was abolished; the princess begged its seat for her office. Because the ground bordered the Luo, she built embankments; lofty terraces and soaring pavilions linked one to another.
translations.idiomatic: She took abolished Yongchang County's seat for her office, embanked the Luo shore, and linked lofty towers.

translations.literal: The cost was no less than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The cost was at least two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 魏王泰故第，東西盡一坊，瀦沼三百畝，泰薨，以與民。

translations.literal: The former residence of the Prince of Wei stretched east and west across a whole ward, with a pond of three hundred mu; when the prince died it was given to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei's mansion had spanned a whole ward with a three-hundred-mu pond; after his death it reverted to the public.

sentences.zh: 至是，主丐得之，亭閣華詭捋西京。

translations.literal: Now the princess begged and obtained it; its pavilions and towers outshone the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: She obtained it; its splendor outdid the western capital.

sentences.zh: 內倚母愛，寵傾一朝，與安樂宜城二主、後郕國崇國夫人爭任事，賕謁紛紜。

translations.literal: Relying inwardly on her mother's love, her favor tilted the court; together with the princesses Anle and Yicheng and the Ladies of State of Hou and Chong she vied for power, and bribery swarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by her mother, she rivaled Princesses Anle and Yicheng and great ladies for power; bribery flourished.

sentences.zh: 東都第成，不及居，韋氏敗，斥慎交絳州別駕，主偕往，乃請以東都第為景雲祠，而西京鬻第，評木石直，為錢二十億萬。

translations.literal: When the eastern capital residence was finished she had not yet lived in it when the Wei clan fell; Shenjiao was demoted to assistant prefect of Jiang Prefecture and the princess went with him. She then requested that the eastern capital residence become the Jingyun Shrine, while the western capital residence was sold and its timber and stone appraised at two billion cash.
translations.idiomatic: Before she could occupy the Luoyang mansion the Wei fell; exiled with Shenjiao, she turned that mansion into the Jingyun Shrine and sold the Chang'an estate for two billion.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年，慎交死，主更嫁蘇彥伯。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan Shenjiao died and the princess remarried Su Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 16 Shenjiao died and she married Su Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 務廉卒坐贓數十萬，廢終身。

translations.literal: Wulian died convicted of embezzling several hundred thousand and was disbarred for life.
translations.idiomatic: Wulian died convicted of embezzling hundreds of thousands and was disbarred for life.

translations.literal: Princess Yongshou was married down to Wei Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yongshou married Wei Huo.

translations.literal: She died young; in the early Chang'an era she was posthumously ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: She died young and was posthumously honored early in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 永泰公主，以郡主下嫁武延基。

translations.literal: Princess Yongtai was married down as a commandery princess to Wu Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yongtai, as a commandery princess, married Wu Yanji.

sentences.zh: 大足中，忤張易之，為武后所殺。

translations.literal: In the Dazu era she offended Zhang Yizhi and was killed by Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazu she offended Zhang Yizhi and Wu Zetian had her killed.

sentences.zh: 帝追贈，以禮改葬，號墓為陵。

translations.literal: The Emperor posthumously ennobled her, reburied her with proper rites, and styled her tomb a mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong posthumously honored her, reburied her with full rites, and called her tomb a mausoleum.

translations.literal: Princess Anle was the youngest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle was the youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 帝遷房陵而主生，解衣以褓之，名曰裹兒。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was moved to Fangling the princess was born; she took off her garment to swaddle her, and named her Wrapped Child.
translations.idiomatic: Born while Zhongzong was exiled to Fangling, she was swaddled in the emperor's own garment and nicknamed Wrapped Child.

translations.literal: Beautiful, clever, and eloquent, the Empress loved her above all.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful and quick-witted, she was the empress's favorite.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wu Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wu Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，光艷動天下，侯王柄臣多出其門。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was restored to the throne, her splendor moved the realm; marquises, kings, and power-holders mostly came from her gate.
translations.idiomatic: After restoration her splendor shook the realm; nobles and ministers flocked to her gate.

sentences.zh: 嘗作詔，箝其前，請帝署可，帝笑從之。

translations.literal: She once drafted an edict, clipped its front, and asked the Emperor to sign approval; the Emperor smiled and complied.
translations.idiomatic: She once drafted an edict, clipped the top, and had the emperor sign it; he laughed and agreed.

sentences.zh: 又請為皇太女，左僕射魏元忠諫不可，主曰：“元忠，山東木強，烏足論國事？

translations.literal: She also asked to be made heir apparent to the throne. Left Vice Minister Wei Yuanzhong remonstrated that it could not be done. The princess said, "Yuanzhong is a stiff Shandong rustic—what does he know of state affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: She sought the title heir apparent; Wei Yuanzhong objected. She said: "Yuanzhong is a stiff rustic—what does he know of state affairs?"

sentences.zh: 阿武子尚為天子，天子女有不可乎？

translations.literal: Even Old Wu's son could become Son of Heaven—why may not a Son of Heaven's daughter?"
translations.idiomatic: Even Wu's son became emperor—why not an emperor's daughter?"

sentences.zh: ”與太平等七公主皆開府，而主府官屬尤濫，皆出屠販，納訾售官，降墨敕斜封授之，故號“斜封官”。

translations.literal: " Together with Taiping and six other princesses she opened offices, but her staff was especially corrupt—all came from butchers and peddlers; they paid fees to sell offices and received appointments by black-edict diagonal seal, and therefore were called "diagonal-seal officials.""
translations.idiomatic: " She and six princesses opened offices, but hers sold posts to butchers and peddlers via sealed edicts—the "diagonal-seal officials."

sentences.zh: 主營第及安樂佛廬，皆憲寫宮省，而工緻過之。

translations.literal: The residences she built and the Anle Buddhist cloister were all copied from the palace offices, yet more finely wrought.
translations.idiomatic: Her mansions and Buddhist cloister copied the palace and surpassed it in refinement.

sentences.zh: 嘗請昆明池為私沼，帝曰：“先帝未有以與人者。

translations.literal: She once requested Kunming Pond as a private pool. The Emperor said, "The late Emperor never gave it to anyone."
translations.idiomatic: She asked for Kunming Pond as a private lake. The emperor said: "My father never gave it away."

sentences.zh: ”主不悅，自鑿定昆池，延袤數里。

translations.literal: " The princess was displeased and dug her own Dingkun Pond, several li in extent.
translations.idiomatic: " Angry, she dug her own Dingkun Pond, several li across.

translations.literal: Ding means that it could rival Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: Ding meant it could rival Kunming.

sentences.zh: 司農卿趙履溫為繕治，累石肖華山，隥彴橫邪，回淵九折，以石瀵水。

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Zhao Lüwen had it constructed; piled stones to resemble Mount Hua, with plank paths crossing in all directions and nine bends around deep pools, using stone channels for water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüwen built it with stone Mount Hua, winding paths, nine bends, and stone aqueducts.

sentences.zh: 又為寶爐，鏤怪獸神禽，間以璖貝珊瑚，不可涯計。

translations.literal: She also made treasure censers, carved with strange beasts and divine birds, inlaid with jade, shells, and coral beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: She added censers carved with mythical beasts and birds, inlaid with jade, shell, and coral beyond count.

sentences.zh: 崇訓死，主素與武延秀亂，即嫁之。
