translations.literal: When Chongxun died the princess had long been having an affair with Wu Yanxiu and at once married him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongxun's death she at once married her lover Wu Yanxiu.

sentences.zh: 是日，假后車輅，自宮送至第，帝與后為禦安福門臨觀，詔雍州長史竇懷貞為禮會使，弘文學士為儐，相王障車，捐賜金帛不貲。

translations.literal: That day she borrowed the empress's carriage and escort from the palace to her residence; the Emperor and Empress watched from Anfu Gate; the metropolitan governor Dou Huaizhen was made master of ceremonies, Hanlin scholars served as ushers, the Prince of Xiang screened the carriage, and gifts of gold and silk were bestowed beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: That day she used the empress's carriage from the palace; the emperor and empress watched from Anfu Gate; Dou Huaizhen directed the rites and gifts poured out.

sentences.zh: 翌日，大會群臣太極殿，主被翠服出，向天子再拜，南面拜公卿，公卿皆伏地稽首。

translations.literal: The next day a great assembly of ministers was held in Taiji Hall; the princess came out in kingfisher robes, bowed twice toward the Son of Heaven, then bowed south toward the ministers, and all the ministers prostrated themselves and knocked their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Next day at Taiji Hall she appeared in kingfisher robes, bowed to the emperor and then to the ministers, who all kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 武攸暨與太平公主偶舞為帝壽。

translations.literal: Wu Youji and Princess Taiping danced in pairs to wish the Emperor long life.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youji and Princess Taiping danced in pairs to wish the emperor long life.

translations.literal: The ministers were granted several hundred thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers received several hundred thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 帝禦承天門，大赦，因賜民酺三日，內外官賜勛，緣禮官屬兼階、爵。

translations.literal: The Emperor attended Chengtian Gate, proclaimed a general amnesty, granted the people three days of mandated feasting, bestowed honors on inner and outer officials, and for those in rites offices granted concurrent ranks and nobility titles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appeared at Chengtian Gate, declared amnesty, gave the people three days of public feasting, rewarded officials, and granted concurrent ranks and titles to rites-office staff.

sentences.zh: 奪臨川長公主宅以為第，旁徹民廬，怨聲囂然。

translations.literal: Linchuan Grand Princess's residence was seized for her mansion; neighboring commoners' dwellings were cleared through, and complaints rang out.
translations.idiomatic: She seized the Linchuan Grand Princess's house for her own mansion, demolishing neighboring homes amid loud public outrage.

sentences.zh: 第成，禁藏空殫，假萬騎仗、內音樂送主還第，天子親幸，宴近臣。

translations.literal: When the mansion was complete, the treasury stores were emptied; the Ten-Thousand Cavalry guard and palace music were lent to escort the princess home; the Son of Heaven personally visited and feasted close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished the treasury was drained bare; imperial guards and palace musicians escorted her home while the emperor visited in person and feasted his close ministers.

sentences.zh: 崇訓子方數歲，拜太常卿，封鎬國公，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: Chongxun's son Fang, only a few years old, was appointed Minister of Ceremonies, enfeoffed as Duke of Hao, with five hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun's son Fang, still a small child, was made Minister of Ceremonies and Duke of Hao with five hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 公主滿孺月，帝、后復幸第，大赦天下。

translations.literal: When the princess had completed her first full month, the Emperor and Empress again visited the mansion and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess completed her first postpartum month, the emperor and empress visited again and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 時主與長寧、定安三家廝臺掠民子女為奴婢，左臺侍御史袁從一縛送獄，主入訴，帝為手詔喻免。

translations.literal: At the time the princess, together with the households of Changning and Ding'an, forcibly seized commoners' sons and daughters as slaves; Left Censorate attendant censor Yuan Congyi bound and sent them to prison; the princess entered to complain, and the Emperor personally drafted an edict ordering their release.
translations.idiomatic: She, Changning, and Ding'an forcibly seized commoners' children as slaves; attendant censor Yuan Congyi had them bound and jailed, but the princess appealed and the emperor wrote a personal edict freeing them.

sentences.zh: 從一曰：“陛下納主訴，縱奴騶掠平民，何以治天下？

translations.literal: Congyi said: "Your Majesty has accepted the princess's complaint and allowed her runners to plunder commoners—how can you govern the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Congyi said: "Your Majesty heeds the princess and lets her runners plunder the people—how can the realm be governed?

sentences.zh: 臣知放奴則免禍，劾奴則得罪於主，然不忍屈陛下法，自偷生也。

translations.literal: I know that releasing the slaves spares me harm while prosecuting them offends the princess, yet I cannot bend Your Majesty's law to save myself."
translations.idiomatic: I know freeing them spares me trouble while prosecuting them offends the princess, yet I cannot bend the law to save myself."

translations.literal: " He did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王誅庶人，主方覽鏡作眉，聞亂，走至右延明門，兵及，斬其首。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linzi executed the commoner, the princess was just at her mirror doing her eyebrows; hearing the chaos she fled to the Right Yanming Gate; soldiers overtook her and cut off her head.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi killed the deposed empress, the princess was doing her eyebrows at the mirror; hearing the uprising she fled to the Right Yanming Gate, but soldiers caught her and beheaded her.

translations.literal: She was posthumously demoted to "Rebellious Commoner."
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously stripped to "Rebellious Commoner."

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，詔以二品禮葬之。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict ordered her buried with second-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong acceded, an edict ordered her burial with second-rank honors.

sentences.zh: 趙履溫諂事主，嘗褫朝服，以項挽車。

translations.literal: Zhao Lüwen fawningly served the princess; he once stripped off court dress and pulled her carriage with his neck.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüwen flattered the princess and once doffed court robes to pull her carriage by the neck strap.

sentences.zh: 庶人死，蹈舞承天門呼萬歲，臨淄王斬之，父子同刑。

translations.literal: When the commoner died, he danced at Chengtian Gate shouting "Long live!"; the Prince of Linzi beheaded him, and father and son suffered the same punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed empress died he danced at Chengtian Gate shouting "Long live!"; the Prince of Linzi beheaded him, and father and son were executed alike.

sentences.zh: 百姓疾其興役，割取肉去。

translations.literal: The people, resenting his conscription of labor, cut flesh from his body.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting his forced labor levies, the people cut flesh from his corpse.

translations.literal: Princess Cheng'an, courtesy name Jijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Cheng'an, courtesy name Jijiang.

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: She was first created Princess of Xinping.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wei Jie.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wei Jie.

sentences.zh: 捷以韋后從子誅，主後薨。

translations.literal: Jie was executed as a kinsman of Empress Wei; the princess died later.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was executed as Empress Wei's kinsman; the princess died afterward.

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong had eleven daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong had eleven daughters.

translations.literal: Princess Shouchang was married down to Cui Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Shouchang married Cui Zhen.

translations.literal: Princess Anxing Zhaohuai died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anxing Zhaohuai died in youth.

translations.literal: Princess Jingshan was married down to Xue Boyang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jingshan married Xue Boyang.

translations.literal: Princess Huaiyang was married down to Wang Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Huaiyang married Wang Chengqing.

sentences.zh: 代國公主名華，字華婉，劉皇后所生。

translations.literal: Princess of Dai, personal name Hua, courtesy name Huawan, was born of Empress Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Dai, named Hua, courtesy name Huawan, was born to Empress Liu.

translations.literal: She was married down to Zheng Wanjun.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zheng Wanjun.

sentences.zh: 涼國公主字華莊，始封仙源。

translations.literal: Princess of Liang, courtesy name Huazhuang, was first enfeoffed as Princess of Xianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Liang, courtesy name Huazhuang, was first created Princess of Xianyuan.

translations.literal: She was married down to Xue Boyang.
translations.idiomatic: She married Xue Boyang.

translations.literal: Princess of Xue was first enfeoffed as Princess of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Xue was first created Princess of Qingyang.

translations.literal: She was married down to Wang Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Shouyi.

translations.literal: Shouyi was executed; she was remarried to Pei Xun.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouyi was executed she remarried Pei Xun.

translations.literal: Princess of Xi was born of Honored Consort Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Xi was born to Honored Consort Cui.

sentences.zh: 三歲而妃薨，哭泣不食三日，如成人。

translations.literal: When she was three the consort died; she wept and would not eat for three days, like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At three, when her mother died, she wept and refused food for three days like a grown person.

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: She was first created Princess of Jingshan.

translations.literal: She was married down to Xue Ji, then to Zheng Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: She married Xue Ji, then Zheng Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 開元初，封邑至千四百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan her fief reached fourteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan her fief reached fourteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 金仙公主，始封西城縣主。

translations.literal: Princess Jinxian was first enfeoffed as Princess of Xicheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jinxian was first created Princess of Xicheng county.

translations.literal: Early in Jingyun she was advanced in enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyun she was promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，與玉真公主皆為道士，築觀京師，又方士史崇玄為師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji she and Princess Yuzhen both became Daoist priests, built an abbey in the capital, and took the adept Shi Chongxuan as master.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiji 1 she and Princess Yuzhen both took vows, built an abbey in the capital, and made Shi Chongxuan their master.

sentences.zh: 崇玄本寒人，事太平公主，得出入禁中，拜鴻臚卿，聲勢光重。

translations.literal: Chongxuan was originally a man of humble origin; serving Princess Taiping he gained access to the inner palace, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and his prestige and power were blazing and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxuan was a commoner who, through Princess Taiping, entered the inner palace, became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and wielded dazzling power.

sentences.zh: 觀始興，詔崇玄護作，日萬人。

translations.literal: When construction of the abbey began, an edict made Chongxuan superintendent; ten thousand men worked each day.
translations.idiomatic: When the abbey was begun, Chongxuan was ordered to supervise it with ten thousand workers a day.

sentences.zh: 群浮屠疾之，以錢數十萬賂狂人段謙冒入承天門，升太極殿，自稱天子。

translations.literal: Buddhist monks resented this; with several hundred thousand in cash they bribed the madman Duan Qian to break into Chengtian Gate, ascend Taiji Hall, and declare himself Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist monks, resenting this, paid several hundred thousand cash to the madman Duan Qian to enter Chengtian Gate, climb Taiji Hall, and proclaim himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 有司執之，辭曰：“崇玄使我來。

translations.literal: When officials seized him, he said in confession: "Chongxuan sent me."
translations.idiomatic: Seized by officials, he confessed: "Chongxuan sent me."

sentences.zh: ”詔流嶺南，且敕浮屠、方士無兩競。

translations.literal: " An edict exiled him to Lingnan and moreover forbade Buddhists and Daoist adepts from competing against each other.
translations.idiomatic: " He was exiled to Lingnan, and an edict forbade Buddhists and Daoist adepts from rivaling each other.

translations.literal: When Taiping was defeated, Chongxuan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping fell, Chongxuan was put to death.

sentences.zh: 玉真公主字持盈，始封崇昌縣主。

translations.literal: Princess Yuzhen, courtesy name Chiying, was first enfeoffed as Princess of Chongchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yuzhen, courtesy name Chiying, was first created Princess of Chongchang county.

sentences.zh: 俄進號上清玄都大洞三景師。

translations.literal: Soon she was advanced to the title Great Master of the Upper Pure Mysterious Capital Three Realms.
translations.idiomatic: She was soon promoted to Great Master of the Upper Pure Mysterious Capital Three Realms.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，上言曰：“先帝許妾舍家，今仍叨主第，食租賦，誠願去公主號，罷邑司，歸之王府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao she submitted a memorial saying: "The late Emperor permitted me to leave the household; yet I still enjoy a princess's mansion and eat from rent and tax—I truly wish to relinquish the princess title, abolish the fief office, and return to the princely house.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3 she memorialized: "The late emperor allowed me to leave the world; yet I still keep a princess's mansion and live on fief income—I wish to give up my title, abolish the fief office, and return to the princely house.

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong refused.

sentences.zh: 又言：“妾，高宗之孫，睿宗之女，陛下之女弟，於天下不為賤，何必名系主號、資湯沐，然後為貴、？

translations.literal: She said again: "I am Gaozong's granddaughter, Ruizong's daughter, and Your Majesty's younger sister—in the world I am not lowly; must I bear the princess title and draw bath-and-income before I am honored?
translations.idiomatic: She added: "I am Gaozong's granddaughter, Ruizong's daughter, and your younger sister—not lowly in the world; must I keep a princess title and fief income to be honored?

sentences.zh: 請入數百家之產，延十年之命。

translations.literal: I ask to renounce the income of several hundred households' estates in exchange for ten years of life."
translations.idiomatic: Let me give up several hundred households' income and gain ten years of life."

translations.literal: " The Emperor understood her true intent and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grasped her meaning and agreed.

translations.literal: She died in the Baoying era.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the Baoying era.

translations.literal: Princess of Huo was married down to Pei Xuji.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Huo married Pei Xuji.

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had twenty-nine daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had twenty-nine daughters.

translations.literal: Princess Yongmu was married down to Wang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yongmu married Wang Yao.

translations.literal: Princess Changfen was married down to Zhang Qushe.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changfen married Zhang Qushe.

translations.literal: Princess Xiaochang died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xiaochang died in youth.

translations.literal: Princess Tangchang was married down to Xue Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Tangchang married Xue Xiu.

translations.literal: Princess Lingchang died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lingchang died in youth.

sentences.zh: 常山公主，下嫁薛譚，又嫁竇澤。

translations.literal: Princess Changshan was married down to Xue Tan, then to Dou Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changshan married Xue Tan, then Dou Ze.

sentences.zh: 萬安公主，天寶時為道士。

translations.literal: Princess Wan'an became a Daoist priest in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Wan'an became a Daoist priest under Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 開元新制：長公主封戶二千，帝妹戶千，率以三丁為限；

translations.literal: New Kaiyuan regulations: grand princesses received two thousand fief households, imperial sisters one thousand, generally capped at three adult males per household;
translations.idiomatic: New Kaiyuan rules: grand princesses received two thousand fief households, imperial sisters one thousand, with a cap of three adult males per household;

translations.literal: imperial princes and kings received two thousand households; princesses received half that.
translations.idiomatic: imperial princes and kings received two thousand; princesses half as much.

translations.literal: Those around him thought this too meager.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers thought this too stingy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“百姓租賦非我有，士出萬死，賞不過束帛，女何功而享多戶邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The people's rent and tax are not mine. A soldier risks death in ten thousand perils—his reward is no more than a bundle of silk. What merit have women that they should enjoy so many households?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The people's taxes are not mine. Soldiers risk death for no more than a bundle of silk—what merit do women have to enjoy so many households?

translations.literal: To let them know thrift—is that not also fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: Should they not learn thrift?"

translations.literal: " Thereupon what the princesses received barely covered carriage and robes.
